panels.rationale: The panel is a clear clinical photograph of a human patient (Patient-5), which the caption explicitly identifies as showing 'Typical facial features of GS,' aligning with the 'Coarse facies' finding in the vocabulary. The image depicts a real human patient with the target disease.

panels.rationale: The image is a pelvic X-ray showing bilateral hip avascular necrosis, which is presented in the context of a case report for Galactosialidosis. The findings align with skeletal manifestations reported for this condition.
panels.attribution_text: Alsahlawi et al. Galactosialidosis: A Report of Three Cases Diagnosed With a Founder Genetic Mutation in the Bahraini Population.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.77750. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Pelvic X-ray of Patient 2 Bilateral avascular necrosis of the hips.
in_text_mentions: Further investigations, including ophthalmology and cardiology reviews, were suggested but not completed, as the patient lost follow-up after the age of 15 years. Additionally, scanogram images of the lower extremities and pelvic X-rays revealed advanced bilateral hip avascular necrosis, indicating the need for total hip replacement (Figure 3). A scanogram of the full spine showed lumbar lordosis (Figure 4).
